new_entities.name: Behavior therapy for preschool ADHD
aliases: behavioral parent-based therapy for preschool ADHD
new_entities.description: Behavioral therapy approaches, often parent-mediated, used as first-line treatment for preschool-aged children with ADHD.

new_entities.name: ADHD severity
new_entities.description: Overall severity of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder symptoms.

edges.effect_quant: A meta-analysis of eight randomized preschool ADHD trials totaling 399 participants found parental behavioral interventions reduced ADHD symptoms with a pooled standardized mean difference of -0.68, while a later randomized trial in 164 preschoolers showed parent training improved parent-rated ADHD and disruptive symptoms compared with wait-list control.
edges.population: preschool-aged children with ADHD or clinically significant ADHD symptoms receiving behavior therapy, usually through parent-mediated treatment
edges.mechanism: Behavior therapy can reduce symptom severity indirectly by improving parent responses, reinforcement patterns, routines, emotional regulation, and disruptive behavior cycles that amplify ADHD symptoms in early childhood.
edges.summary: Behavior therapy is one of the strongest nonpharmacologic options in preschool ADHD and is appropriately treated as first-line care. The effect is not universal or dramatic in every child, but the pooled evidence supports meaningful symptom reduction, especially on parent-rated measures.
edges.caveats: Teacher-rated and objective laboratory effects are often smaller than parent-rated improvements. The main benefits are usually symptom and family-function gains rather than full remission.

evidence.citation: Mulqueen JM et al 2015 J Atten Disord
evidence.notes: Meta-analysis: parental interventions for preschool ADHD.

evidence.notes: Parent training for preschool ADHD: a randomized controlled trial of specialized and generic programs.
